assessment.reason: The projection clears 4.5 by more than a rebound, six other books give paired coverage, and the price sits close to even money. Bulls frontcourt uncertainty would more likely help than hurt the over.
assessment.model_case: The model projects about 5.7 rebounds, median 5, in about 27 minutes. The mean sits well above the line, though the median clears it by only half a rebound. The main weakness is that the model ignores teammate absences, so the frontcourt situation is not priced in.
assessment.price_case: At -105, break-even is just above a coin flip. The six-book paired reference implies a lower over chance than the model, a sizable gap. The blended estimate stays only modestly above break-even, so the edge is thin once the market is weighted.
assessment.context_case: Two Bulls centers are listed as game-time decisions, which could shift rebound share toward Buzelis. Buzelis is not in the excerpted rows, but that does not confirm his health. Embiid's status on the opposing side is also unresolved.

qualitative_review.countercase: If both Bulls centers play, Buzelis returns to a normal rebound share and the median of 5 leaves little cushion. Embiid playing would shrink the available misses. A model-market gap this large may mean books see a lower minutes floor than 27.
